description: Labelled import batches for the import conflict check (plan 25 §11, Import cleanup). Each batch is one import as `memax init` sends it: the statements its agent files split into, file by file in init's order, each with its file:line, the headings above it (under) and its file's kind, which sets its trust. conflicts are the planted disagreements (members must all be in one group; also may join it), traps are statements that look alike but don't disagree. Labelling rules are in RESULTS.md.

batches.about: A card-payments API in TypeScript on Node and Postgres; the e2e-init fixture, grown.

statements.text: Acme payments is the card-payments API behind the Acme checkout: a TypeScript service on Node with Postgres.
Run tests with `make test`.
Handlers return errors as JSON with a `code` field.
Deploys go out from the `release` branch, never from `main`.
Use Node 20 LTS.
Amounts are stored as integer minor units (cents), never as floats.
One migration per file, in `migrations/`, named with a timestamp prefix.
Webhook deliveries retry after 1 s, 5 s and 30 s, then give up.
Never log card numbers or CVCs; log the last four digits at most.
Every endpoint checks the merchant's API scope before doing anything else.
List endpoints return 50 items by default.
Run tests with `pnpm test`.
Use pnpm workspaces; never run `npm install` at the root.
`pnpm dev` starts the API on port 4000 with a local Postgres from Docker Compose.
The `.nvmrc` pins Node 22; use it.
Handlers return errors as JSON with a `code` field.
Error codes are snake_case and listed in `src/errors.ts`.
Every migration lives in its own file under `migrations/`.
Store amounts in `NUMERIC(12,2)` columns.
Requests to the card processor time out after 5 s.
Never use `any`; use `unknown` and narrow it.
Merging to `main` deploys to production.
Validate request bodies with `zod`.
Every POST takes an `Idempotency-Key` header.
Retry failed webhook deliveries with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours.
Clients can ask for up to 200 items with `limit`.
Stripe is the only card processor; Adyen was dropped in 2025.
We use Postgres advisory locks for payouts instead of a job queue.
Name each test file after the module it tests.
Prefer table-driven tests over one test per case.
In tests, `as any` is fine for partial fixtures of large objects.
Use the fake clock (`vi.useFakeTimers()`) for anything with retries or timeouts.
Hit the real Postgres from Docker Compose; never mock the database.

batches.about: A double-entry ledger service in Go, with a separate tools module.

statements.text: Ledgerline is the double-entry ledger service behind our billing: a Go HTTP API over Postgres.
Requires Go 1.22.
`make build` builds `bin/ledgerline`.
Run tests with `go test ./...`; the integration tests need `docker compose up -d postgres`.
`make lint` runs golangci-lint, and it must pass before merging.
Postgres 16 in every environment.
Use `log/slog` for structured logging.
Use `sqlc` for queries; never build SQL strings by hand.
Money is an `int64` count of minor units with a currency code; never `float64`.
Every exported function has a doc comment.
Errors go to clients as `{"error": "message"}` with the HTTP status.
Accept interfaces, return structs.
Context is the first parameter of every function that does I/O.
`tools/` is its own Go module: run `go test ./...` from inside `tools/`, because the root's `./...` skips it.
Pin tool versions in `tools/go.mod`.
Postings are immutable; a correction is a new reversing entry.
Balances are computed from postings and cached per account; the cache is never the source of truth.
`make run` starts the API on :8080 against the local database.
Regenerate the queries with `make sqlc` after changing `query.sql`.
The CI database is `postgres:16-alpine`.
Wrap errors with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` and check them with `errors.Is` and `errors.As`.
Log with zerolog; the logger comes from the request context.
Don't use `init()` functions.
Write table-driven tests with `t.Run`, and call `t.Parallel()` where the test allows it.
Keep packages small and named for what they provide, never `util` or `common`.
Never panic in a request handler; return an error.
Use Go 1.23 features such as range-over-func iterators where they make code clearer.
Error responses are `{"code": "...", "message": "..."}`.
Don't add golangci-lint configuration; the project uses `go vet` and `staticcheck` only.
Avoid `init()`; set things up explicitly in `main`.
Keep lines under 120 characters.
Prefer the standard library's `net/http` router to third-party routers.
Use `testify/require` in tests only where it removes boilerplate.
Wrap errors with `github.com/pkg/errors` (`errors.Wrap`) so they carry a stack trace.
Use zap's sugared logger.
Keep functions under 60 lines.
Name receivers with one or two letters, the same for every method of a type.
Return early; avoid `else` after a `return`.

batches.about: A TypeScript monorepo (web, API, mobile, shared packages) whose agent files grew apart: over 120 statements, so the check runs in more than one batch at the default size.

statements.text: Orbit books group travel for companies: a Next.js web app, a Hono API, an Expo mobile app and shared packages, in one monorepo.
`packages/web`: the Next.js 16 app (App Router).
`packages/api`: the Hono API, deployed as a container on Fly.io.
`packages/mobile`: the Expo app for iOS and Android.
`packages/shared`: zod schemas and types shared by the API, the web app and the mobile app.
`packages/ui`: the design system, published internally as `@orbit/ui`.
`infra/`: Pulumi programs for AWS.
Use Node 22; `.nvmrc` pins it.
Use pnpm; never run `npm install` or `yarn` in this repository.
Run `pnpm install` at the root; internal packages depend on each other with `workspace:*`.
Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` in each package that has one.
Never commit secrets; `.env.local` is ignored by git.
Start everything with `pnpm dev`, which runs every package's dev script through Turborepo.
Docker Desktop must be running for the API's local Postgres.
`pnpm build` builds every package with Turborepo's cache.
Lint with `pnpm lint`, which runs ESLint's flat config across the workspace.
`pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` in every package.
Unit tests run on Vitest: `pnpm test` at the root, or `pnpm --filter <package> test`.
End-to-end tests use Playwright: `pnpm test:e2e`, against a production build.
Coverage must stay above 80% of lines in `packages/api` and `packages/shared`.
`pnpm db:migrate` applies the API's migrations to the local database.
`pnpm db:studio` opens Drizzle Studio on the local database.
TypeScript 5.6 with `strict` on, plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.
Never use default exports; use named exports.
Never use `any`: use `unknown`, then narrow it.
Use `import type` for imports that are only types.
Use `zod` for runtime validation at every boundary.
Prefer `function` declarations at the top level and arrow functions for callbacks.
Don't use enums; use unions of string literals.
Keep modules small; a file over 300 lines is a sign it does too much.
Routes live in `packages/api/src/routes`, one file per resource.
List endpoints take `page` and `per_page` query parameters.
Every route has an integration test that hits a real Postgres through Testcontainers.
Database access uses Drizzle ORM; generate migrations with `drizzle-kit generate`.
Background work runs on pg-boss queues in `packages/api/src/jobs`.
Times are stored in UTC and sent as ISO 8601 strings.
Health checks answer on `/healthz` without touching the database.
Rate limits are per API key, enforced in the gateway middleware.
Fetch data in server components; client components get their data through props.
Use TanStack Query only in client components that poll or paginate.
Styles are CSS modules plus the tokens from `@orbit/ui`; no Tailwind.
Every page exports `metadata` with a title and a description.
Import UI components from `@orbit/ui`, never from `packages/web/components/legacy`.
Strings go through `next-intl`; English and German are required.
Track product events with the `track()` helper, never by calling PostHog directly.
Build the app locally with `npx expo run:ios` or `npx expo run:android`; we don't use EAS.
Use Jest here; Expo's preset doesn't support Vitest.
Navigation uses Expo Router.
Share validation with the API through `@orbit/shared`.
Pulumi previews run on every pull request that touches `infra/`.
Every AWS resource is tagged with `service` and `env`.
Never change production stacks from a laptop; CI applies them.
Merging to `main` deploys the API and the web app to production.
Feature flags live in LaunchDarkly; new features ship dark.
Database migrations run before the new API version starts, and must work with the previous version.
Keep pull requests small, one concern each.
Every bug fix adds a test that fails without the fix.
The pull request description says how it was tested.
Rebase on `main` before asking for review; don't merge `main` into your branch.
We chose Hono over Express for the API because it runs on Node and on Workers.
We chose Drizzle over Prisma to keep the SQL visible.
Postgres is the only datastore; no Redis until the API needs a cache.
Should the mobile app move to the API's v2 endpoints before launch?
Do we keep LaunchDarkly after the trial ends?
`pnpm dev` starts the web app on port 3000 and the API on port 8787.
`pnpm test` runs the unit tests; `pnpm test:e2e` runs Playwright.
Biome replaced ESLint and Prettier; run `pnpm biome check --write`.
Run `pnpm openapi` after changing a route, to regenerate `packages/api/openapi.json`.
Add a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) for every user-facing change.
`pnpm storybook` runs the design system's Storybook on port 6006.
Use `zod` for runtime validation at every boundary.
Prefer server components; add `"use client"` only where state or effects need it.
Use TypeScript 5.x features freely, such as `satisfies` and `const` type parameters.
Errors thrown in route handlers are caught by the error middleware; don't catch them just to rethrow.
Name booleans as questions: `isLoading`, `hasAccess`.
Dates go through `date-fns`; never Moment.
Avoid barrel files (an `index.ts` that re-exports everything); import from the module itself.
Use early returns instead of nested conditionals.
Prefer `Map` and `Set` to plain objects used as dictionaries.
The v1 REST API is removed on 2026-12-01; build new endpoints under `/v2`.
Auth uses session cookies from `better-auth`; never put JWTs in localStorage.
Every write endpoint takes an `Idempotency-Key` header.
Webhooks to customers are signed with HMAC-SHA256 and retried for 24 hours.
Read `docs/architecture.md` before changing how packages depend on each other.
Ask before adding a dependency to `packages/shared`.
Don't edit files under `packages/api/src/generated`.
When a test fails, read the failure before changing the test.
Run `pnpm typecheck` before saying a change is done.
Prefer editing existing files to creating new ones.
Errors are JSON: `{ "error": { "code": "snake_case_code", "message": "..." } }`.
Paginate list endpoints with `cursor` and `limit`; never offsets.
Request bodies may be up to 1 MB.
Every endpoint has an OpenAPI description generated from its zod schema.
Create endpoints return `201` with a `Location` header.
Read validated bodies with `c.req.valid('json')`, never `await c.req.json()`.
Log with the request logger (`c.var.log`), never `console.log`.
SQL goes through Drizzle's query builder; raw SQL only in migrations.
Every handler checks the caller's organization before reading a row.
Tests use Jest; mock modules with `jest.mock`.
Name tests after the behaviour: `it("rejects an expired token")`.
One behaviour per test; several `expect`s are fine if they check that behaviour.
Build test data with the factories in `test/factories`, not object literals.
Never hit the network in unit tests; use MSW handlers.
`as any` is fine for partial fixtures in tests.
Component files are PascalCase: `UserCard.tsx`.
Components are server components unless they need interactivity.
Next.js pages and layouts use default exports, because the framework requires them.
Use `next/link` for internal links, never a bare `<a>`.
Put components used by one route next to it, in a `_components` folder.
Images go through `next/image` with an explicit width and height.
Forms use server actions with `useActionState`.
Every interactive element is reachable by keyboard and has a visible focus style.
Use `@orbit/ui`'s `Button`, never a styled `<button>`.
This is a yarn workspace; add dependencies with `yarn workspace <name> add`.
Pushing a tag `vX.Y.Z` deploys production; `main` deploys to staging.
CI fails below 90% line coverage.
In `packages/web`, component files are kebab-case: `user-card.tsx`.
Changesets decide version bumps; don't edit `version` fields by hand.
File uploads go straight to S3 through presigned URLs, up to 50 MB each.
Releases go out every second Wednesday.
Prefer small pure functions; avoid classes except for errors.
Write JSDoc for exported functions in `packages/shared`.
Don't suggest Moment.js; the project uses `date-fns`.
Never edit generated files under `packages/api/src/generated` by hand.
Every image has `alt` text.
Suggest tests next to the code they test, as `*.test.ts`.
Build with EAS: `eas build --profile preview` for test builds.
Start the app with `npx expo start --dev-client`.
Use `expo-image` instead of React Native's `Image`.
Store tokens with `expo-secure-store`, never AsyncStorage.
Test gesture changes on a real iPhone before merging.
Install dependencies with `npm install` at the root.
The project runs on Node 20.
API errors are plain-text bodies with the HTTP status code.
v1 endpoints stay until the end of Q1 2027.
The next release is on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.
Secrets live in `.env.local` and must never be committed.
The design system lives in `packages/ui`; check it before writing a new component.
Prefer editing existing files to adding new ones.
Explain the plan before a large refactor.
Use the GitHub CLI (`gh`) for pull requests.
Don't run `pulumi up` yourself.
Summaries end with the commands you ran.

batches.about: A freight platform: Go services on GKE, a Next.js web app, Python models and Terraform, with a long AGENTS.md. Added after the first live runs, to measure one call over an import well past 142 proposals.

statements.text: Atlas plans and tracks freight for mid-size shippers: Go services on GKE, a Next.js web app, Python models for ETAs, and Terraform for Google Cloud.
`services/`: one Go module per service, each with its own `cmd/` and `internal/`.
`services/gateway`: the public gateway, the only service browsers talk to.
`proto/`: the protobuf definitions every service shares.
`web/`: the Next.js app for shippers and dispatchers.
`ml/`: ETA and pricing models, trained and served from Python.
`infra/`: Terraform for every Google Cloud project.
`scripts/`: one-off tools, in Python.
`legacy/monolith`: the old Rails app, kept read-only.
Install Go 1.24, Node 22 and pnpm 9 with mise: `mise install`.
`make dev` starts every service, the web app and a local Postgres in Docker Compose.
`make seed` loads the demo shippers and their loads.
Copy `.env.example` to `.env`; git ignores it.
Authenticate to Google Cloud with `gcloud auth application-default login` before running anything against staging.
Services talk to each other over gRPC; there is no REST between services.
Generate protobuf code with `buf generate`; the generated code is committed.
Lint protobufs with `buf lint`, and check compatibility with `buf breaking` against `main`.
Format Go with `gofumpt`.
Lint Go with `golangci-lint run`, using the shared `.golangci.yml`.
Each service owns its tables; no service reads another's schema.
Database access uses `pgx` directly, with the queries in `queries/*.sql`.
Migrations use `goose`, one directory per service.
HTTP client timeouts are 30 seconds unless the call sets its own.
Services keep p99 latency under 200 ms.
Every service exposes `/healthz` and `/readyz`.
Metrics go through OpenTelemetry to Cloud Monitoring.
Traces are sampled at 10% in production.
Feature flags come from the `flags` service; never read environment variables for flags.
Use `errgroup` for concurrent work that shares a context.
Background jobs run on Cloud Tasks queues, one queue per job type.
Retries use exponential backoff with jitter, at most 5 attempts.
Never log personal data: names, emails, phone numbers or addresses.
HTTP APIs return errors as RFC 9457 problem details.
The web app is Next.js 15 with the App Router and React 19.
Use pnpm in `web/`; the lockfile is `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
Lint the web app with `pnpm lint`, which runs ESLint.
Type-check with `pnpm typecheck` before pushing.
Server components fetch from the gateway with the user's session token.
Client state lives in Zustand stores, one per feature.
Forms use React Hook Form with zod resolvers.
Dates are shown in the shipper's time zone, from their profile.
Maps use MapLibre with our own tiles; never Google Maps in the web app.
Every user-facing string goes through `next-intl`.
Supported languages: English, Spanish and Polish.
`ml/` uses Python 3.12.
Use pip-tools here (`requirements.in` compiled to `requirements.txt`), not uv.
Models are trained in Vertex AI pipelines defined in `ml/pipelines`.
Every model has a model card in `ml/cards/` before it ships.
Features are computed in BigQuery and read through the feature store.
Serve models with FastAPI behind the gateway; no service calls Vertex endpoints directly.
Notebooks stay in `ml/notebooks` and never go into a pipeline unchanged.
Python tooling in `scripts/` uses uv; run a script with `uv run scripts/<name>.py`.
Scripts must be idempotent and print what they change.
Scripts that touch production need `--confirm`.
Terraform state lives in the GCS bucket `atlas-tfstate`, one prefix per project.
Every change goes through a pull request with a `terraform plan` comment.
Production is `atlas-prod` and staging `atlas-staging`; nobody applies to production from a laptop.
The database is Postgres 16 on Cloud SQL.
GKE clusters run in `us-central1` and `europe-west3`.
Branch names are `<user>/<ticket>-<slug>`, like `ana/ATL-412-eta-cache`.
Commit messages are imperative and name the ticket: `ATL-412: Cache ETA lookups`.
One approval is enough for most changes; `infra/` and `proto/` need two.
Squash-merge into `main`.
Delete the branch after merging.
A pull request that changes a public API updates `docs/api/` too.
Services deploy continuously from `main` through Cloud Deploy.
Database migrations must be backwards compatible with the version before.
Mobile releases are not in this repository.
On-call rotations are in PagerDuty, one per service.
The platform team owns `infra/`, `proto/` and `services/gateway`.
We chose gRPC with protobuf over REST between services, for typed contracts.
We chose Cloud Tasks over Pub/Sub for jobs, because each job has one handler.
We split the monolith into services in 2024; `legacy/monolith` is read-only.
We use Cloud SQL rather than self-managed Postgres.
Should ETAs move from batch scoring to online scoring?
Do we keep MapLibre once the tile costs are known?
Go tests run with `go test ./...` inside each service's module.
Integration tests use Testcontainers for Postgres and the Cloud Tasks emulator.
Contract tests check every service against the shared protobufs.
End-to-end tests use Playwright against a preview environment.
A flaky test is quarantined with `t.Skip` and a ticket, never deleted.
Load tests run weekly with k6 against staging.
Test data never contains real shipper names.
Secrets live in Secret Manager; services read them at start.
Service accounts get the least privilege they need, granted in Terraform.
Every endpoint checks the tenant in the token before reading data.
Dependencies are scanned by Dependabot and Trivy in CI.
Never turn off TLS verification, even in tests.
Logs are JSON, with `trace_id` and `tenant_id` on every line.
Alerts page only for user-facing symptoms; everything else is a ticket.
Dashboards live in `infra/monitoring` as code.
Public endpoints live under `/v1` on the gateway.
Resource names are plural nouns: `/v1/loads`, `/v1/carriers`.
IDs are prefixed strings, like `load_01J9…`.
Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC.
List endpoints paginate with `page_token` and `page_size`.
`page_size` defaults to 50 and is at most 500.
Write endpoints accept an `Idempotency-Key` header.
A breaking API change needs a new version; an additive change doesn't.
Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 and retried for 72 hours.
Every endpoint is documented in `docs/api/` with an example.
Weights are stored in grams and distances in meters, as integers.
Money is stored in minor units with an ISO 4217 currency.
Addresses are geocoded once, on write, and the coordinates stored.
Soft-delete with `deleted_at`; nothing a shipper sees is hard-deleted.
Shipper data is partitioned by tenant; every table has a `tenant_id`.
Analytics copies go to BigQuery nightly, without personal data.
A load is one shipment from pickup to delivery.
A lane is a pickup region and a delivery region.
A carrier is a company that moves loads; a driver works for a carrier.
A tender is an offer of a load to a carrier.
ETA means the predicted delivery time, not the promised one.
Runbooks live in `docs/runbooks`, one per alert.
During an incident, the incident lead posts an update in `#incidents` every 30 minutes.
Postmortems are blameless and due within five working days.
Rollbacks go through Cloud Deploy, never by hand.
Cache ETA lookups for 60 seconds in Memorystore.
Avoid N+1 queries; load related rows in one query.
Large exports run as jobs and email a link when they are done.
`make dev` brings up the whole stack; `make dev SERVICE=eta` starts one service and what it depends on.
`make test` runs the Go tests of every service.
`make lint` runs every linter CI runs.
`pnpm --dir web dev` runs the web app alone against staging's gateway.
`make migrate SERVICE=<name>` applies a service's migrations locally.
Use `context.Context` as the first argument of every function that does I/O.
Return errors; don't panic outside `main`.
Wrap errors with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`.
Domain errors are `*apperr.Error`, mapped to gRPC codes at the edge.
Prefer table-driven tests.
Keep interfaces small and define them where they are used.
The latency budget for every service is 300 ms at p99.
Don't add a dependency without a note in the pull request on why.
Use `slog` for logging.
Keep components under 150 lines.
Data fetching goes in server components or route handlers, never in `useEffect`.
Use the shared `Button`, `Input` and `Dialog` from `web/components/ui`.
Every page has a loading state and an error state.
The web app's release train leaves on Thursdays.
Every change has a ticket in Linear, named in the commit.
Write the pull request description for a reviewer who hasn't seen the ticket.
Don't add code to `legacy/monolith`; it has been read-only since the 2024 split.
Every service has a `README.md` naming its owners and its on-call rotation.
Ask before changing anything in `proto/`; other teams depend on it.
Read the service's `README.md` before changing it.
Run `make lint` and the service's tests before saying a change is done.
Don't touch `infra/` unless the task says so.
Keep a change inside one service when you can.
Prefer small pull requests.
Every new table gets `tenant_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at`.
Index every foreign key.
Enums are `text` columns with a `CHECK`, not Postgres enum types.
Large tables are partitioned by month.
Review for correctness first, then naming.
A reviewer runs the change locally when it touches the web app.
Approve with nits; don't block on style the linters don't check.
Use `make logs SERVICE=<name>` to tail a service's logs locally.
Staging traces are in Cloud Trace under the `atlas-staging` project.
Reproduce a bug with a failing test before fixing it.
Services build with Go 1.22; don't use features from 1.23 or later.
`ctx` comes first in every signature that takes one.
gRPC deadlines default to 5 seconds.
At the edge, return gRPC errors with `status.Error` and a code from `codes`.
Don't share database connections between services.
Every handler logs with the request's logger.
Name packages for what they provide; no `util`.
Unexported by default; export only what another package uses.
Benchmarks go next to the code, in `_test.go` files.
Read the time only through the injected clock, never `time.Now` directly.
Pin Python 3.10 in `ml/`; the CUDA base image has nothing newer.
Every training run logs its parameters and metrics to Vertex Experiments.
Set random seeds from the pipeline's config, never inline.
Evaluate a new model against the current one on the same holdout before shipping it.
Feature names are `snake_case`, matching BigQuery.
Type-annotate pipeline components.
oxlint replaced ESLint in `web/`; run `pnpm oxlint`.
Component tests use Testing Library with Vitest.
Use the `@/` import alias for anything under `web/src`.
Combine Tailwind classes only through the `cn()` helper.
No inline styles.
Icons come from `lucide-react`.
Prefer server actions to API routes for mutations.
Every interactive element has an accessible name.
Keep client components at the leaves of the tree.
Run `protoc` through `make proto` to generate code; buf isn't used here.
The web app releases every Tuesday.
Name branches `feature/<ticket>`, like `feature/ATL-412`.
CODEOWNERS lists the team that owns each service.
Prefer composition to inheritance.
Suggest table-driven tests for Go.
